title: Cut Athena job wall time: measure phases, land three speedups
summary: Measure where Athena job wall time goes, using the records of jobs since 2026-10-23. Then implement the three largest avoidable cuts, likely land trusting Athena's recorded checks on the exact PR tree, parallel independent plan-group jobs, and a faster full test suite. Document the breakdown, the cuts, their alternatives and the before and after medians in docs/decisions.md, with tests for each cut.

defaults_applied.how: Every cut has tests, and cargo test and clippy must pass.
Measured numbers are marked measured and others are labeled as estimates in decisions.md.
Criteria check that landing accepts or rejects candidates correctly, not just that the wiring exists.
The outcome is lower median wall time, stated before and after. It is not the activity of editing.
Decision entry records chosen cuts with alternatives, including reuse of existing crates for parallelism.
Negative tests show that skipped CI never lets a failing candidate land.
Code and docs are written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: cut Athena's end-to-end job wall time. The audience is the Athena owner, who reads docs/decisions.md and judges by the before/after medians.

records/ is absent from my copy. I assume the producer or Athena supplies the job timing data, and the measured breakdown is built from it. If the producer cannot read records, it must say so and not invent numbers.

The three cuts are assumed to be: (1) land accepts Athena's own recorded fmt/clippy/test result on the PR's exact tree instead of waiting for CI, where host rules allow; (2) parallel execution of independent jobs in a plan group; (3) a faster full test suite. The measurement may reorder these, and the decision entry would then say why.
The 'after' median needs jobs run after the change lands. The verifier cannot produce them, so that figure may be recorded as pending or added later.
This is one large change. Splitting would be better, but the request lists these files together.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/decisions.md has a new entry with a per-phase wall-time breakdown (reading, planning rounds, producer runs and send-backs, Athena's checks, verifier, landing/CI) marked 'measured, from the records' for jobs since 2026-10-23. It gives job counts and medians, and labels any figure not measured as an estimate.
The entry names the three largest avoidable costs chosen and, for each cut, the alternatives considered and why they were rejected.

Each cut has at least one new test that passes under `cargo test`. These include: land accepting Athena's recorded checks only when they match the PR's exact tree; parallel running of independent plan-group jobs; and the full-suite speedup.

Negative tests show no failing candidate can land through a cut. A recorded check that failed, is missing, or is for a different tree still blocks landing or falls back to waiting for CI. Dependent jobs are never run in parallel. Check with `cargo test`.
`cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

docs/decisions.md states the median job wall time before, and after measured on jobs run after the change. If no post-change jobs exist yet, it says so explicitly and leaves the after value as pending. It does not invent a number.

CHANGELOG.md lists the three cuts in plain language. Any .github/workflows/ci.yml change is named in the decision entry and keeps fmt, clippy and test required for any path that does not use Athena's recorded checks.

out_of_scope: Changing the planner or reader prompts.
Removing or weakening any fmt, clippy or test check for candidates without a matching recorded result.
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, or branch protection and host rules.
Changes to records/ or owner files.
departures: This request is much larger than the typical job. It covers three code cuts, tests, measurement from records and docs, and it needs host-rule judgment about CI. I raised cost and time, and lowered the chance of a pass. The 'after' median cannot be verified immediately.
